task: D6.1 manager-authoritative submission read/clear boundaries without legacy fallback
decision: Manager is the only production business execution module for migrated submission routes. /api/dex/submissions/detail and /api/dex/submissions/clear no longer read or write legacy SQLite. They call manager_api only, return structured manager errors when manager is unavailable, and fail closed instead of silently reverting to legacy. Existing UI direct business reads are being converted into test oracle/fixture material rather than a runtime fallback.

implementation.pendingAttemptClearRejection: InvalidRequest: cannot clear broadcast records while pending attempts exist
implementation.dryRunPolicy: dryRun=true counts and reports without deleting or writing idempotency records
implementation.idempotencyPolicy: same idempotency key and same digest replays the persisted clear result
implementation.transactionPolicy: apply runs idempotency lookup, pending check, counts, deletes, state reset and write-request audit in a single IMMEDIATE transaction

architecturePolicy.uiDirectReadsConvertedToTestOracle: only after the corresponding manager DTO route exists; detail and clear are already converted

fixtures: broadcast clear apply is dry-run safe
broadcast clear is idempotent and rejects same key with a different digest
broadcast snapshot status filter is applied before offset and limit
manager API HTTP route enforces X-Request-Id, Idempotency-Key, explicit dryRun and manager authority
Flask clear route calls the manager adapter and never calls _submission_database_url
Flask clear route reports manager_unavailable without legacy sqlite fallback
template clear button posts JSON to /api/dex/submissions/clear with recordKind=submission and dryRun=false
architecture guard rejects load_cow_execution_attempt_detail, manager_ui_data_source and clear_cow_execution_attempts_sqlite in migrated submission route module
knownBoundary: D9.8 covers manager-authoritative submission detail/clear and manager-owned terminal broadcast reads. Summary, category, review-success/review-failed and overview routes still contain legacy SQLite projection paths for production data and are the next migration unit. No mainnet manager apply, broadcast, service restart, or destructive data operation was performed.
